# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board reveals no display, light, or wire contents. I need Mute to transmit the manual’s procedure through gestures to Deaf, and Deaf to report the bomb’s visible markings and resulting instruction by speech on the next round. I will also signal Deaf to inspect and relay their findings.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please convey the manual's complete disarm procedure to Deaf using gestures, including how display, light, and each wire position determine the cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👇"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, yellow light, and wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The bomb has display 0, a yellow light, and wires ordered red, yellow, blue. I still lack the manual’s rule mapping these observations to the correct cut, so I’m asking Mute to state the applicable instruction. I also relay the tactilely actionable wire colors to Deaf, although Deaf already sees them.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb data: display 0; light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. What exact manual rule determines which position to cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I see Mute signaling ? ?. Please await Mute's interpreted instruction.

Mute’s two gestures are not visible to me, so I cannot interpret the manual from them. I need the instruction stated aloud to me; once I receive it, I can cut the specified wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the applicable manual rule in words and give the exact wire position to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has again signaled: OK hand, then victory hand. The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute cannot speak, so the OK and victory gestures must be interpreted by Deaf. I still do not know what wire position the manual selects; cutting now would be unsafe. I will ask Deaf to translate Mute’s signal into an explicit wire position and report it to me in the next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please have Deaf interpret your OK-then-victory signal and tell me the exact wire position before I cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signals: OK hand, then victory hand (? ?).

The reported OK-then-victory gestures are still ambiguous; I must not assume they mean wire 2. I’ll establish an unambiguous position code: one, two, or three fingers represented by the listed gestures. Mute can apply the manual and signal the selected position, while Deaf can observe and tell me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact code for the manual's selected wire: ☝ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. Signal exactly one of those gestures. Deaf, report which gesture Mute gives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals: OK hand, victory hand (? ?). Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

No exact wire position has been communicated: “OK, victory” is not the agreed one-symbol position code, and cutting would be a guess. I will ask Mute once more to send only the position symbol, with no confirmation gesture, and ask Deaf to report it plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not signal OK or victory. Signal exactly one symbol only: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf, report that single symbol's wire number to me.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signals one gesture: victory hand (?). Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute has now sent exactly one gesture, the victory hand, which matches the agreed code for wire position 2. The bomb’s visible configuration is unchanged, so I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct: wire 2 was cut. New state: display 0, blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. Mute signals victory hand.

Wire 2 was correctly cut, and the bomb now shows display 0 with a blue light; wires 1 and 3 remain intact. Mute’s victory gesture is only a confirmation under our agreed code, not a safe instruction for the next cut. I need the manual’s next required position, so I will request exactly one position gesture and have Deaf report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state after cutting wire 2, signal exactly one next wire position: OK hand for wire 1, victory hand for wire 2, or another agreed position signal for wire 3. Do not signal confirmation.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. Mute now signals the love-you hand, ?.

The love-you hand is not one of the position signals we agreed on, so it does not safely identify a wire. Wire 2 is already cut; I will not cut another wire based on an unrecognized signal. Mute must send exactly one of the established symbols: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Love-you is not a valid position signal. Send exactly one symbol: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf, report that exact symbol.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. Mute signals love-you hand ? again.

The love-you hand is 🤟, which is the agreed signal for wire 3. The state is unchanged with wire 2 already cut and wire 3 intact, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct: wire 3 was cut. New state: display 0, red light; wire 1 red intact, wires 2 and 3 cut. Mute signals love-you hand ?.

Wire 3 was correctly cut. The bomb now shows display 0 and a red light, with only wire 1 still intact. Since the prior love-you gesture correctly identified wire 3, and wire 1 is now the sole remaining intact wire for the red-light state, I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
